text:
sasha: customer reported malformed JSON in structured mode when their input includes embedded control chars (\n, \r, and some U+FFFD-looking sequences). app fails to parse and downstream job retried -> extra billing + latency spike. attaching minimal payload we used to repro. ticket created: INC-4832 :exclamation:

maria: can you drop the request_id and sample output? also which SDK (node/python) and model+version?

sasha: node SDK, model: gpt-open-16k-v1, structured: true, streaming: true. request_id: r-9a7c. sample chunk that breaks is in the last batch, looks like this when concatenated:
```
...\"text\": \"hello\\u0000world\\nline2\\udc00\\udc01\"
```
parser throws EOF/invalid escape depending on client parser.

ty: hmm those are unpaired surrogates (\udc00) in the payload. we usually normalise to \uFFFD or escape as UTF-16 surrogate pairs. are these coming from the customer input or from the model?

sasha: customer pasted some logs via copy/paste. includes NULs and weird windows CRLFs. they expect structured mode to produce valid JSON though.

engineer-miguel: quick note: with streaming + chunk boundaries we sometimes split an escape sequence across chunks which makes client-side incremental JSON parsers choke. common repro: enable streaming, send a long string with a backslash at the chunk boundary. Workarounds: 1) disable streaming, 2) enable an escape-safe serializer on our side, or 3) recommend the client use tolerant incremental JSON parser.

engineer-miguel: minimal repro (node):
```js
const res = await client.completions.create({
  model: 'gpt-open-16k-v1',
  input: { mode: 'structured', prompt: 'A:\n\u0000B\\nC\udc00' },
  stream: true
});
// then concat chunks and try JSON.parse -> fail
```

maria: can you attach server logs for r-9a7c? want to check if our encoder emitted lone surrogates or if they came through raw.

support-bot: created ticket INC-4832 assigned to eng-runtime. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4832

billing-ops: customer says they were double-billed because client retried on parse failure. can we do a one-off credit while we investigate?

ingrid: SRE saw a latency blip from 2026-10-03T14:22:xxZ matching the ticket. routing shows many of these requests were served on a node with kernel 5.x and older glibc; possible serializer differences. I'll capture heap and network dumps for those hosts.

ty: immediate mitigation: add a server-side post-process step that escapes lone surrogates and control characters before emitting chunks. low-risk toggle: enable \"escape_control_chars\": true for structured streaming. will prototype and roll to staging.

engineer-miguel: also add a patch to chunk boundaries to avoid splitting escape sequences (buffer 4 bytes lookahead). that will reduce incremental parser errors.

sasha: I'll ask the customer for their client stack and offer temporary non-streaming endpoint and a goodwill credit.

maria: plan: 1) repro + confirm origin (customer vs server) 2) quick toggle to escape control chars in streaming 3) patch chunking logic 4) billing adjustment if confirmed. assigning owners: ty (mitigation), ingrid (infra dumps), billing-ops (credit).

billing-ops: ok will draft credit note once you confirm token counts.

sasha: thanks everyone. pinging here for updates. :pray:
